nodes.statement: A BBSSD write request is submitted with an exclusive ending LBA beyond the namespace size.
femu_nvme_rw_check_req compares elba to nsze and treats elba greater than nsze as out of range.
The write enters FEMU's NVMe I/O command dispatch and request-validation path.
The BBSSD I/O dispatch routes the request between the NVMe poller and FTL processing rings.
The submission queue removes a request object from its free request list for this command.
The NvmeRequest carries the command status while it traverses the poller and FTL rings.
The out-of-range validation records an error-page entry and sets NVME_LBA_RANGE with NVME_DNR.
Because the request status is not NVME_SUCCESS, the FTL loop skips every opcode handler.
The failed request is still enqueued through the FTL completion ring with its carried error status.
The FTL loop assigns zero added latency and returns the failed request to the poller.
After posting completion, the poller returns the request object to the submission queue free list.
The guest observes a completion queue entry carrying the original out-of-range error.
The source oracle requires out-of-range rejection, skipped FTL mutation, CQE posting, and request return.

edges.statement: The submitted write computes an elba that is checked against the namespace nsze bound.
The out-of-range request reaches the NVMe I/O entry where read/write validation runs.
NVMe I/O dispatch hands the BBSSD request into the poller-to-FTL call chain.
The poller dispatch operates on a request object acquired from the submission queue.
The acquired NvmeRequest owns the command and its validation status through completion.
Validation mutates the owned request status after recording the out-of-range error page.
The non-success status prevents the FTL loop from invoking write, read, or trim handlers.
Skipping opcode handling preserves the carried status for completion-ring propagation.
The failed request traverses the to_poller ring with zero FTL latency for cleanup completion.
The poller posts completion and returns the cleaned request to its free list.
Returning the request follows posting the error-bearing CQE visible to the guest.
The source oracle binds the CQE error and request release to the out-of-range validation result.

disconfirming_checks.statement: A request whose status already failed validation must not enter ssd_write or any other FTL opcode handler.
